newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Asset swap seen as one option for JCI, Lonrho.
newsitem.headline: Asset swap seen as one option for JCI, Lonrho.

text.p: South Africa's JCI Ltd and British conglomerate Lonrho PLC were still discussing future cooperation despite calling off merger talks being on Monday, industry sources and analysts said.
"The company confirms that it has been approached to discuss other possible transactions, which could unlock value for shareholders in both JCI Ltd and Lonrho," JCI said in statement.
Industry sources speculated the companies were now looking at asset swaps.
An industry source said JCI's unlisted Tavistock coal division could be swapped for Lonrho's 33.6-percent stake in Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd , one of the most succesful gold producers in Africa.
The source said most analysts saw Lonrho as keen to acquire JCI's coal assets while JCI would want Lonrho's Ashanti stake.

Analysts said the swap could open the way for JCI to enter into a deal with Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd in which JCI could swap the Ashanti stake for Anglo's stake in Lonrho, which the European Union has told it to reduce.
Anglo desperately wants a stake in Ghana's Ashanti and said last week that Lonrho had suggested swapping its stake in Ashanti for Anglo's Lonrho shares.
The South African mining giant said it would support a merger between JCI and Lonrho but stressed it did not initiate the merger talks.
After pressure from the European Commission (EC), Anglo said in April it would cut its 27-percent stake in Lonrho to less than 10 percent.
The EC said Anglo and Lonrho's combined platinum interests with that of another South African company, Gencor Ltd , would constitute a monopoly of the world platinum industry.
Lonrho holds substantial interests in two South African platinum mines.
Analysts said they believed the JCI/Lonrho talks, aimed at creating a global mining house with a market capitalisation of some $3 billion, were called off because JCI's price was too high.
"As the transaction went on, it became unrealistic. The deal floundered on price," Investec Securities analyst John Clemmow said.
He said Lonrho's mining operations were relatively small. The company is trying to reorganise and dispose of its non-core hotel and African trading operations.
"When Lonrho Africa and the general trade division have gone, Lonrho mining will have a life that is nasty, brutish and short," he said, making it a prime takeover target.
